thread:
maria: Quick sync — follow-up on the postmortem action items from last week's span-loss + aggregator-lag incident. I want ownership/timelines for the items we promised to deliver this sprint.

jon: I own the 'missing spans' instrumentation task. Working on adding a sampling sanity check and a retry metric. Will PR today.

samira: I can take the ETL backfill plan for the mis-aggregated counters. ETA end of week if no blockers. Need to know exact time windows we want to backfill. @linda can you confirm analytics windows?

linda: Yes — focus on 2026-03-10 00:00 to 2026-03-12 23:59 UTC first. Those are the ranges product reported noise.

alex: I'll pair with Jon on the KV cache path where we saw truncated spans during high load. Suspect race around cache invalidation + serializer.

maria: Great. Can everyone confirm estimated delivery dates as YYYY-MM-DD? Also we should add a recurring check to detect this pattern.

jon: 'missing spans' instrumentation PR today (2026-03-23). Tests and deploy by 2026-03-24.

samira: Backfill plan doc by 2026-03-24, run and validate by 2026-03-26.

alex: Fix branch by 2026-03-25, can canary on dedicated pool 2026-03-26.

linda: Dashboard alerts updated by 2026-03-24 to pin the windows.

maria: Assigning formal owners in the tracker: jon -> OBS-317, samira -> ETL-672, alex -> RUNTIME-209. I'll add to the postmortem follow-up board.

deploy-bot: Created issue OBS-317 (jon), ETL-672 (samira), RUNTIME-209 (alex) — links: https://redwood.internal/ops/OBS-317, https://redwood.internal/ops/ETL-672, https://redwood.internal/ops/RUNTIME-209

jon: Quick Q — for the instrumentation check, do we prefer a counter that increases when span size > X or a timer for serialization failures?

alex: Counter + last-failure-tags is simplest and cheap. Also emit the request-id and sequence-id for tracing.

samira: For backfill validation, can we reuse the agg-e2e harness? I can point it at the historical S3 partitions.
linda: Yes reuse harness — add a diff check that compares pre- and post-backfill aggregates with tolerances.

maria: Action items recap (short):
- jon: implement span sampling sanity + metric (due 2026-03-24) (OBS-317)
- alex: fix cache invalidation race + canary (due 2026-03-26) (RUNTIME-209)
- samira: backfill + validate mis-aggregated counters (run by 2026-03-26) (ETL-672)
- linda: update dashboards/alerts and provide verification windows (done 2026-03-24)

maria: Also want to add a recurring monitoring job (weekly) that looks for these three signals: span count drop, aggregator delta spikes, ETL lag > 5m. Who can own that?

jon: I can wire up span-count drop alert into observability, but need someone to own ETL lag metric.

samira: I'll own the ETL lag check and put a weekly job in the ETL ops calendar.

alex: I'll add an automated regression test in runtime CI that simulates high QPS and ensures no span truncation.

linda: Once backfill runs, I'll review analytics and sign-off on whether product metrics are restored.

maria: OK — sounds good. Please update the issues with links to PRs and retrospecs when ready. We'll re-check on next incident-review meeting (2026-03-30).

jon: Will do. Filing PR now. :thumbsup:

samira: Backfill plan doc at https://redwood.internal/docs/ETL-672-backfill.md — feedback welcome.

alex: Allocated time to pair on Monday 9am PT.

deploy-bot: OBS-317 status changed -> in_progress by jon

maria: Thanks team. If anyone hits blockers, ping me and I'll help escalate.

linda: :raised_hands:

alex: noted.

jon: PR merged, will kick canary after smoke tests. (2026-03-24 15:10 UTC)

samira: Backfill started (2026-03-26 02:05 UTC) — small validation mismatch, investigating thresholds.

maria: Filing follow-up note for the next roundup with the threshold decision.

linda: After backfill validation, product metrics look within tolerance. Closing ETL-672 once samira confirms final diff.

samira: ETL-672 closed. Added notes about tolerances and the weekly ETL lag monitor runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/etl/weekly-lag-monitor.md

maria: Marking this thread resolved for the sprint. We'll include the actions in the 2026-03-30 incident review. Thanks everyone! :party:
